concepts.title: Source Documents and Accounting Vouchers
concepts.definition: Written proofs of financial exchanges such as cash memos and bills serve as source documents, from which formal accounting vouchers are prepared to authorize debit and credit entries.
concepts.key_idea: Every business entry must be supported by verifiable documentary evidence arranged chronologically.
question_patterns: what is a source document

explain source documents and accounting vouchers

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the exchange involves cash payment, cash receipt, or a non-cash adjustment.

A transaction with one debit and one credit uses a transaction voucher; multiple debits with one credit or vice versa uses a compound voucher; multiple debits and credits use a complex or journal voucher.

concepts.title: Fundamental Accounting Equation
concepts.definition: A mathematical statement demonstrating that total economic resources owned by an entity always equal the sum of claims held by external lenders and internal owners.
concepts.key_idea: Dual-aspect accounting ensures the equality of resources and financing claims at all points in time.

calculate fundamental accounting equation for the given values

solution_steps.explain: Total assets must equal total claims consisting of liabilities and proprietor equity.

concepts.title: Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation
concepts.definition: Calculating an unknown component of the balance sheet equation by isolating either capital or liabilities from total assets.
concepts.key_idea: Owner's residual equity equals total assets less outsider claims.

concepts.title: Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment
concepts.definition: Closing capital is derived by adjusting beginning capital with operational revenues, business expenses, fresh funds invested, and withdrawals made by the proprietor.
concepts.formula: closing_capital = opening_capital + fresh_capital + revenue - expenses - drawings
concepts.key_idea: Revenues and fresh capital expand equity, whereas expenses and drawings diminish it.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract expenses from revenue to get net operating addition to capital.

concepts.title: Modern Rules of Debit and Credit
concepts.definition: The system governing account entries: assets and expenses increase by debit and decrease by credit, whereas liabilities, capital, and revenues increase by credit and decrease by debit.
concepts.key_idea: Debits increase asset and expense balances; credits increase liability, capital, and revenue balances.

solution_steps.explain: Classify the account into one of the five categories: Asset, Liability, Capital, Expense, or Revenue.
Debit for increases in assets/expenses or decreases in liabilities/capital/revenue; credit for decreases in assets/expenses or increases in liabilities/capital/revenue.

concepts.title: Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry
concepts.definition: Recording financial events chronologically in a five-column journal format specifying debited accounts, credited accounts, amounts, and explanatory narrations.
concepts.key_idea: Every journal entry preserves the dual-aspect equality by having identical aggregate debit and credit sums.

concepts.title: Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation
concepts.definition: Computing Goods and Services Tax wherein intra-state supplies are taxed equally as Central GST and State GST, while inter-state supplies are subject to Integrated GST.
concepts.formula: cgst = base_amount * cgst_rate / 100; sgst = base_amount * sgst_rate / 100; invoice_total = base_amount + cgst + sgst
concepts.key_idea: Intra-state purchases split GST equally between CGST and SGST, whereas inter-state trade levies full IGST.

concepts.title: Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit
concepts.definition: Offsetting the input tax credit paid on procurement against output tax collected from customers to compute the net tax payable to the government.
concepts.key_idea: The government receives only the value-addition tax, computed as output tax minus eligible input tax credit.

concepts.title: Ledger Accounts and Posting Mechanism
concepts.definition: Transferring debits and credits recorded in chronological journal entries to individual analytical ledger accounts to summarize balances.
concepts.key_idea: Posting organizes transactions by individual accounts in the principal book to determine balances at any given time.

concepts.title: Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts
concepts.definition: Calculating the portion of debt recovered in cash versus the irrecoverable loss written off as bad debts when a debtor is declared insolvent.
concepts.formula: recovered_amount = total_debt * recovery_rate / 100; bad_debts = total_debt - recovered_amount
concepts.key_idea: Dividend from an insolvent debtor's estate is debited to cash/bank and the remaining deficit to bad debts account.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the total outstanding debt by the percentage or paise-per-rupee dividend received.

solution_steps.action: compute irrecoverable loss written off as bad debts
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the recovered amount from total outstanding debt.

concepts.title: Computation of Interest on Capital
concepts.definition: Determining the interest allowable to the proprietor on capital invested in the business for a specific time period at a stated annual percentage rate.
concepts.key_idea: Interest on capital is treated as a business expense and increases the owner's total capital claim.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply principal capital by annual rate and months, dividing by 1200.
